chapter: Coming up in New York and Harlem theatres
title: Director of music at the Lafayette and Apollo, and discovering Ella and Sarah Vaughan
summary: He becomes theatre music director in 1930, claims to have discovered Ella Fitzgerald for Chick Webb and Sarah Vaughan for Earl Hines, and lists big bands at the Apollo.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Well, how do you explain that. We all know that, but how do you -- I know you worked with him all these years. And we haven't even got into that, because we've
got plenty of time to talk about your association with him. When did you find out about him being a master.

I went with -- I'm ahead of the story but in 1930, I went into the theatre, see, director of music. At the Lafayette, we went from the Lafayette into the Harlem Opera House, that's when I discovered Ella Fitzgerald and I introduced her to Chick Webb. Chick Webb exploit her, but I discovered her.
I discovered her and told Chick about it and that's when Chick and -- what's his name? -- Al, anyway Chick took her over and he exploited her. She became great.

And then we went -- we only stayed in the Harlem Opera House about three or four months and then we moved into the Apollo and see we had amateur night, see, and I used to rehearse everybody, get the key and everything.
I remember that because I was there.
And play for them and we went into the Apollo Theatre and Sarah Vaughan was on this night, Earl Hines was the band, so I said to Earl --

This was in '30. And I said to Earl, hey, we got a kid here that can really sing, so she won the contest that night and Earl took her right away and then in '31 Jimmie Lunceford come to town and he made good and then

Erskine Hawkins' band came in and then Stuff Smith he came in, see, and they all started call the big bands and Harry James, this is at the Apollo Theatre, Harry James came in. What's the guy that died, trumpet player, just died. Louis Prima.
